title: Hyperbolic thermoelasticity: A review of recent literature
unified_law: Section 5 treats a unified approach to ETE and TRDTE; Section 6 describes Green-Naghdi theory as a limiting case of ETE; Section 7 surveys memory, semi-empirical-temperature, and dual-phase-lag theories.
geometries_covered: Section 6 illustrates the Green-Naghdi theory with boundary-initiated waves in a half-space.
experimental_evidence: Section 2 reports thermal-relaxation measurements in materials and processed meat; these are not direct validation of thermoelastic-wave predictions.
limitations: The 1998 appraisal describes anisotropic work as very small (especially for TRDTE), nonhomogeneous studies as almost nonexistent, memory work as receiving little attention, nonlinear theory as very meager, TEWOED physical relevance as unresolved, and dual-phase-lag theory as nascent.

title: Thermoelasticity without energy dissipation
unified_law: Type-II thermoelasticity without energy dissipation is developed for nonlinear and linear response; in the linearized theory, the same potential determines stress and entropy flux, permits finite-speed thermal waves, and supports a uniqueness theorem.
thermodynamic_restrictions: The linearized theory obtains a specific-heat condition from Second-Law inequalities and says no additional Second-Law restrictions follow because internal entropy production is zero; the general discussion says further restrictions are not recorded here.
geometries_covered: General finite-body continuum; linearized theory assumes isotropy and treats an initial mixed boundary-value problem through a uniqueness theorem.
